feedback.answered: Initial source-only backbone, not a readiness declaration. A1: the leader assigns term/index to admitted proposals, appends to its unstable log and schedules its own append acknowledgement through msgsAfterAppend. Followers qualify append support against log history; leader progress is aggregated through the configured voter quorum, with joint configurations requiring both constituent majorities. raft.maybeCommit additionally requires a matching current-term entry. Append-response commitment advancement broadcasts the decision and releases pending ReadIndex requests. Ready exposes committed entries to the caller; persistence, application and transport are explicitly caller duties. A2: campaign admission checks promotability and unapplied committed configuration changes. Elections use log freshness, term/vote qualification and configured vote aggregation; pre-vote changes candidacy without incrementing the term. Term dispatch rejects stale ordinary messages and steps down for applicable newer terms. reset clears vote aggregation, progress, transfer state and readOnly support, while preserving log history. Newly acquired leadership appends a current-term empty entry and conservatively delays configuration proposals behind its previous log tail. Connection: support is interpreted under current term and voter configuration, while established committed history survives authority changes. Storage responses are not all equivalent: append stabilization responses carry the issuing term to prevent stale completion from truncating a rewritten unstable log; snapshot completion remains applicable across term changes because it represents committed state. RawNode creates another append completion on changed HardState while unstable entries remain, addressing the specific concern that rejecting an old completion necessarily leaves the unstable log forever retained. These are implementation observations and stated caller contracts, not executed evidence or a proof of the whole protocol.
remaining: Core readiness still requires following snapshot restore and restart reconstruction, configuration changer entry/exit semantics, and Node serialization/completion paths. The source trace above does not externalize these unread in-repository responsibilities.

Sourced continuation lead at raft.appliedTo: automatic leave proposals are rejected while leadTransferee is set; its comment expects a later applied-entry/advance retry if transfer fails. tickHeartbeat aborts a timed-out transfer without directly invoking appliedTo. Determine whether a legal application/transfer ordering can consume the final relevant apply response during transfer and leave no owed retry trigger after abort; inspect all alternative callers and applicable automatic-transition contract before constructing an obligation.

Sourced consumer difference at raft.switchToConfig: successful maybeCommit broadcasts append, whereas the MsgAppResp path also calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages. Determine whether a legal configuration application can cause the first current-term commitment while reads are pending and whether another consumer releases them. Current-term commitment guard and later append responses are counterevidence; input legality and caller ordering are not established.

reset reconstructs readOnly but does not visibly reset pendingReadIndexMessages in the inspected range. Trace the queue producer, release function and response context contract before deciding whether retained requests are intentional retryable work or an authority-context discrepancy.
